name: IconButton
label: Icon button
description: Icon-only button in primary, secondary and tertiary emphasis and a default, neutral or destructive tone, in default and compact sizes.

props.name: icon
props.description: The icon — Material Symbol name (string) or custom element (ReactNode)

props.name: variant
props.description:
Emphasis: `primary` (filled), `secondary` (outlined) or `tertiary`
(ghost). The colour is `tone`'s job. `neutral` is the legacy value from
before the split and renders as `variant="primary" tone="neutral"`.

props.name: tone
props.description:
Colour, independent of emphasis: `default` carries the action colour,
`neutral` the greys, `destructive` the danger colour. Tertiary is
already grey, so `neutral` leaves it unchanged; a tertiary
`destructive` takes the outlined look, since a danger action needs a
visible edge.

props.name: priority
props.description: Legacy alias for `variant`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the button is disabled

props.name: state
props.description: Documentation-only interaction state.
props.deprecated:
Use `disabled` for the disabled state.

Documentation-only affordance for rendering a *static* interaction state in
Storybook and the showcase site. Real hover/active styling comes from CSS
pseudo-classes and needs no prop — for docs, prefer
`className="ds-icon-button--hover"`.

props.name: size
props.description: Button size

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a spinner in place of the icon and blocks interaction while an
async action runs. Keeps the variant's full-colour appearance (unlike
the disabled state) and sets `aria-busy` on the rendered element.

props.name: label
props.description:
The button's name: what a screen reader announces and, by default, what
the tooltip shows. Required, because the button has no visible text.
Named as Button's and AiButton's text is, so the family spells it one way.

props.name: tooltip
props.description:
The hover/focus tooltip. An icon-only control names itself: by default
the button wears a Tooltip carrying `label`. Pass a string to show
different wording, or `false` to opt out — for a host that labels the
control another way, or one that owns the button's box directly
(SplitButton's trigger stretches to its sibling segment, which the
tooltip wrapper would block).

props.name: tooltipPosition
props.description: Which side the tooltip opens on. `start` and `end` follow the reading direction.

props.name: href
props.description: Optional href — renders as <a> instead of <button>

props.name: target
props.description: Optional target attribute for links

props.name: rel
props.description: Optional rel attribute for links

props.name: badge
props.description: A mark on the button's top-end corner, as BottomNav draws one: a count (a notification bell's unread), or `true` for a dot with no number.

props.name: badgeMax
props.description: The highest count the badge spells out; a larger one reads "99+". Defaults to 99.

props.name: badgeLabel
props.description:
Text read after `label` while the button carries a badge, given the
badge. Defaults to ", new" for a dot and ", 3 new" for a count; the
leading comma and space are part of the text. The tooltip keeps
`label` alone.
props.defaultExpression: (badge: number | string | true) => (badge === true ? ', new' : `, ${badge} new`)

props.name: locale
props.description: The BCP 47 locale a numeric badge is written in, such as `ar-EG`. Defaults to `en-US`. This component can render from a Server Component, so it takes the prop alone and reads no LocaleProvider.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes

props.name: linkComponent
props.description:
The component the link renders with, such as Next.js's `Link`, so it
navigates through the app's router; a plain `<a>` when unset. This
component can render on the server, so it never reads a LinkProvider:
pass the prop even under one.

LinkComponent.description: A component that renders a link in place of a plain `<a>`, such as a router's.

LinkComponentProps.description:
The props a link component receives: every anchor attribute, the ref, and
an `href` that is always a string. Next.js's `Link` takes these as they
are; a router whose link takes `to` instead needs a one-line adapter:
`({ href, ...props }) => <RouterLink to={href} {...props} />`.

alternatives.name: Button
alternatives.when: the action needs its words on show, with or without an icon beside them

alternatives.name: CopyButton
alternatives.when: the button puts a value on the clipboard and should confirm it
